subject: Kestrel hosted API: expected monthly tokens + 99th TPS sanity check
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kestrel hosted API: expected monthly tokens + 99th TPS sanity check

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today, Alex — really appreciate the context on the personalization use case. Quick recap and the few items we promised to follow up on: 

- You said production launch target: October 2028.
- Primary workload: personalized article generation (prompt length ~450 tokens; expected output avg ~850 tokens).
- Current staging QPS: ~20 rps; anticipated production 99th percentile spikes up to ~750 TPS in short bursts (1–3 minute windows) during peak business events.

Can you confirm the expected average monthly token consumption range (input + output) and the realistic peak sustained TPS you want Redwood to guarantee (99th percentile over 1m window)? If you can share a quick CSV snapshot of current staging traces, that would help us size a recommended slab and pricing band.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will sketch three hosted-tier pricing options (conservative / balanced / aggressive) with clear $/1M token guidance and burst capacity assumptions. Karthik will validate 99th TPS SLO implications for the billing and dedicated capacity (if you prefer reserved).

Thanks — Logan

--
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0189
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@kestrel.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Jun 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel hosted API: expected monthly tokens + 99th TPS sanity check

Logan — thanks for the follow-up. Quick answers below and I attached a short usage snapshot as requested.

- Monthly token estimate: 120M–220M tokens/month (this includes retries and analytics CTAs).
- Typical burst profile: baseline 60 TPS with event-driven bursts to ~750 TPS (these are 90–180s windows, observed maybe 2x/week).
- Budget range: early product stage, internal target $/1M tokens is ~$65–$95. We have flexibility if latency is tight at peak.

Attachment: kestrel_usage_snapshot.csv (sample traces, 7-day window)

Let me know if you need anything else to make the proposal concrete. Happy to sync this week.

—Alex
Head of Platform 
Kestrel AI
alex.wu@kestrel.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@kestrel.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Jun 2028 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel hosted API: expected monthly tokens + 99th TPS sanity check

Alex — thankful for the snapshot, that helps a lot. High-level interpretation from our sizing run:

- Token arithmetic: at 170M tokens/month (midpoint), with your prompt/output split the average request is ~1,300 tokens.
- Concurrency profile: the 750 TPS spikes will push tail latency unless we provide burst-friendly routing and a small dedicated reserve.

Attached is a draft pricing options PDF that maps to your stated $/1M target. Summary (very abridged):

1) Conservative (Host Basic): $95 / 1M tokens, soft-burst to 900 TPS using best-effort pooling (no SLA on 99th).
2) Balanced (Host Plus): $78 / 1M tokens, includes 99th p99 SLO at 750 TPS with warm prefix caching and pre-warmed burst lanes.
3) Aggressive (Host Premium): $65 / 1M tokens, 99th SLO at 750 TPS with reserved burst and expedited kernel lanes + 24/7 ops on-call (requires 6mo commit or heavier month-to-month rate).

Notes: pricing above assumes no per-request transformations and standard tokenization. If you want lower unit cost, a Dedicated commit (reserved capacity) can drop the effective $/1M by ~18–27% depending on commit length and t-shirt size.

Next ask: can you confirm whether Kestrel prefers a soft SLA (no credits) or required 99th SLO with financial credits? Also, are you open to a 6-month pilot commit to secure the Premium band?

Thanks — Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@kestrel.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel hosted API: expected monthly tokens + 99th TPS sanity check

Looping in a couple of quick sizing/ops clarifications from the runtime side: 

- If we price to the Balanced band at $78 / 1M and Kestrel lands at 170M tokens/month, monthly bill = ~$13,260. If you plan to push close to 220M, it becomes ~$17,160. We’ll include a delta for sparse cache warmups during start-of-burst.
- Operationally, to hit 99th at 750 TPS we recommend maintaining a 15–20% headroom reserve in our hosted pools. That can be met via a short-duration burst buffer rather than long-term Dedicated capacity.
- If Kestrel wants the Premium $65/1M band with the SLO, require a 6-month commit (monthly commit amount TBD; propose starting at 150M tokens/month commit).

I’ll prepare a quick SLO note (impact to headroom / suggested monitoring hooks) and share it with you by Monday.

—Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@kestrel.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel hosted API: expected monthly tokens + 99th TPS sanity check

Appreciate the detailed options. Quick decisions from our side: 

- We’re comfortable starting with Balanced (Host Plus) at $78 / 1M tokens and a 3-month pilot. Goal is to validate peak handling and billing cadence.
- We’ll target a soft commit: 150M tokens/month for months 1–3 (with a 20% overage tolerance for launch month). If the pilot looks good, we’ll convert to a 6-month Premium commit to get to the $65 band.
- Confirming: we’ll sign an NDA addendum and a short SOW. Our procurement team (purchasing@kestrel.ai) will send a PO and the contact for the DocuSign routing.

Next steps requested of Redwood:
1) Draft a 3-month pilot SOW and pricing addendum reflecting the 150M/month commit and $78 / 1M pricing, include burst handling notes and SLO expectations (non-financial credits).
2) Share a DocuSign link once the SOW is ready.
3) Karthik — please share the SLO note you mentioned.

I’ll loop in procurement after we have the SOW. Thanks all.

—Alex

--
